triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120) risks the '22. Preprocess cache is not valid when the contract says recompute every execution' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 22. Preprocess cache is not valid when the contract says recompute every execution

problem.statement: GDN Chunk Forward Pitfalls (CuTeDSL, SM120) -- 22. Preprocess cache is not valid when the contract says recompute every execution

payload.attempted: Cache K0/K_inv outputs because benchmark inputs are often repeated during profiling. This makes the fast path look attractive: K1 dominates wall time, and preprocess tensors are deterministic for a fixed input.
payload.lesson: Treat preprocess cache, CUDA graph/static replay, and FLA fallback as separate system-level features, not kernel acceptance optimizations. For this target, the only valid stop line is the full 3-kernel no-cache path.

established_fact.mechanism: K0 and K_inv are part of the GDN forward computation for the current input. Caching them changes the measured operation from "run GDN" to "run K1 using stale preprocessed state." That hides memory traffic and launch work that production must pay whenever q/k/g/beta changes.

payload.observed: Invalid acceptance path. The clarified target requires K0 preprocess q/k normalization, K_inv beta-fold / Neumann intermediates, and K1 output/final_state to run every execution. V113 meets the target without that shortcut: `0.531-0.533 ms` vs FLA `0.804 ms`, about `1.51x`.
payload.root_cause: K0 and K_inv are part of the GDN forward computation for the current input. Caching them changes the measured operation from "run GDN" to "run K1 using stale preprocessed state." That hides memory traffic and launch work that production must pay whenever q/k/g/beta changes.
